messages.subject: my_RW code (page 88 of the manual)
parts:
Hi guys:

I was looking at this example code because I want to write my own proposal distribution keeping everything else as is. If I understand correctly the command: 

proposal <- norm(1,model[[target]],scale) 

can be changed to any distribution. For example, if I have multiple target nodes, it can be a multivariate normal distribution of dimension equal to the number  of random effects plus the number of hyper-parameters. Or, some other distribution can be used here as long as it has the correct dimension. 

There are two questions:

a) Does it have to be one of the standard distributions or can I use something else such as mixtures of normals say or product of gamma distribution for one parameter and mixture of univariate normal distributions for the other hyper parameters?

b) The acceptance probability depends on the form of the proposal distribution and not just the distribution of the random effects and hyper parameters. But the Metropolis step described later in the function seems to not have proposal distribution density. 

I am sure I am missing something obvious. I am not too facile in computing. Thanks for your help.

Subhash Lele

messages.author: 99aa11b224ba9e9e
messages.subject: Re: my_RW code (page 88 of the manual)
parts: Subhash, thanks for your email.  I'm happy to see you're interested in writing your own sampler function in NIMBLE!  Please keep in touch with how it works, and any more questions you might have along the way.  Let me address your questions.

>> proposal <- norm(1,model[[target]],scale) 
>> can be changed to any distribution. For example, if I have multiple target nodes, it can be a multivariate normal distribution of dimension equal to the number  of random effects plus the number of hyper-parameters. Or, some other distribution can be used here as long as it has the correct dimension.

Yes, exactly right.  You could use any multivariate distribution here (of the correct dimension), or any combination of values generated from different distributions.  In that case, you could individually add elements of the proposal vector (e.g., proposal[1:k] ) one at a time, or in blocks:
proposal[1:3] <- ....
proposal[4] <- .....
etc..

>> a) Does it have to be one of the standard distributions or can I use something else such as mixtures of normals say or product of gamma distribution for one parameter and mixture of univariate normal distributions for the other hyper parameters?

No, it does not need to be one of the standard distributions.  Yes, you could use a mixture of normal distributions.  If you want the mixture distribution to vary (i.e. not be fixed), then you could use other model nodes to define properties of the mixture distribution.  In that case, the control list argument can be used to supply the model node names which defined properties of the mixture.

>> b) The acceptance probability depends on the form of the proposal distribution and not just the distribution of the random effects and hyper parameters. But the Metropolis step described later in the function seems to not have proposal distribution density.

Correct.  The example shown doesn't include the proposal density since it's a symmetric normal distribution.  To correctly implement your sampler, you would have to calculate the forward and backward proposal densities (which can use calls to standard R density functions, i.e. dgamma()), then include this additive terms in the MH ratio calculation:
log_MH_ratio <- model_lp_proposed - model_lp_initial + backward_proposal_logdensity - forward_proposal_logdensity
(forgive me if I have the +/- signs wrong)

Good luck!  Let us know if you have other questions.

Cheers,
Daniel
